1. The most frequent symptoms of primary ciliary dykinesia (PCD) are: neonatal respiratory distress, recurrent respiratory infections, bronchiectasis, asthma, sinusitis, and infertility.

the presence of at least one of the five indicators of a reduced CBF (situs inversus, bronchiectasis, recurrent pneumonia, retention of airway secretion, and neonatal respiratory disorder) is a good predictor of a reduced Ciliary beat frequency (OR 6, 95% CI: 4.1-9.1, p=0.0001).

in patients with chronic cough, a reduced ciliary frequency can be detected by a simple questionnaire, which includes questions on neonatal respiratory disorder, situs inversus, retention of airway secretion, recurrent pneumonia, bronchiectasis, asthma with poor response on treatment.

the development of a questionnaire to preselect patients for further investigation in a specialized centre.
the development of an algorithm for the preselection of children with a high probability for primary ciliary dykinesia.
a questionnaire to preselect patients for primary ciliary disease.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the presence of at least one of the parameters mentioned above in a patient with chronic cough is a strong indicator for a reduced CBF, whereas the absence of any of these parameters in a patient with a chronic cough is a good indicator for a normal CBF.

a reduced CBF should be considered if at least two of the following features are present in a patient with chronic cough: neonatal respiratory disease, situs inversus, retention of airway secretion, recurrent pneumonia, bronchiectasis, asthma with poor response.

the presence of one or more of the above mentioned features in a patient with chronic cough is an indication for the search of a reduced ciliated beat frequency, which is an indication for a primary ciliary dyskinetic disorder.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the presence of at least one of the following parameters in a patient with chronic cough is highly indicative of the presence of primary ciliary dykinesia: neonatal respiratory disorders, situs inversus, retention of airway secretion, recurrent pneumonia, bronchiectasis and a poor response to bronchodilators.
we have found a way to preselect patients for further investigation in a specialized centre.

in patients with a chronic cough and no other cause of cough, a reduced Ciliary Beat Frequency (CBF) is highly unlikely if the patient has none of the following findings: neonatal respiratory disorders, situs inversus, retention of airway secretion, recurrent pneumonia, bronchiectasis, and poor response to treatment of asthma.
The main takeaway from our work is that
we have identified a set of clinical features that, if present, should raise suspicion that an individual has primary ciliary dyskenesia.
we have developed a questionnaire that can be used by physicians to identify patients with primary ciliary dyskenesia.
we have developed a questionnaire to preselect patients who have a high probability of having a cilia defect.
